title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Water Supply"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Water supply is built one component at a time. Hydropower direct use is complete and is what
`water_supply_gep` currently carries. A water-use calculation covering agriculture, industry and
municipal withdrawals is ported and reported beside it as separate columns. The price convention
recorded in `es_config.csv` is `resource rent (CWoN 2024)`, and the base year is 2019.

## Hydropower

### Quantity and price

The hydropower valuation has no separate quantity and price step. CWoN 2024 publishes a
capitalised hydropower wealth per country, and the annual rent that wealth implies is what the
account wants.

### Valuation

`annuity_factor` is the present value of one dollar a year over the CWoN horizon,

$$
A = \sum_{t=1}^{100} \frac{1}{(1+r)^t}, \qquad r = 0.04
$$

and `hydropower_rent_from_wealth` divides each country's `YR2019` wealth by it. Countries without
wealth stay NaN, because no data is not zero rent.

The method was identified by reverse-engineering against the drive's committed 2019 output, whose
script is not on the drive. It is exact across all 94 valued countries, with the ratio constant to
1e-10. The test suite asserts the annuity identity and the exact replication. An earlier
direct-use script on the drive, price times quantity from EIA and World Bank series dated November
2024, is superseded by this method and is not ported.

## Water use

### Quantity and price

Withdrawal volumes in cubic metres per sector come from the withdrawal table. The price is the
AQUASTAT SDG 6.4.1 water-use efficiency series in US dollars per cubic metre, one series per
sector.

### Valuation

`clean_aquastat_water_efficiency` is script 01 of the drive's R calculation. It keeps the US$/m3 rows of
the four SDG 6.4.1 series and pivots them wide by country and year.

`water_use_gep_by_country_year` is script 02. It applies three country renames onto the withdrawal
table's spellings, fills iso codes for the names its country map does not carry, drops the
regional aggregate rows, merges the two tables, restricts to the survey years, and multiplies
efficiency by withdrawal per sector to give `gep_water_agricultural`, `gep_water_industrial` and
`gep_water_municipal`.

`water_use_components_from_chain` takes the latest survey year per country and keys it to r250 by
exact country-name match, first on `iso3_r250_name` and then on `name_long`. A calculation country with
no match keeps an empty iso3, so a name drift is visible instead of dropped.

Both of the R calculation's own outputs replicate. The cleaned efficiency table matches bit-exactly. The
country-year GEP table matches to the anchor CSV's own 15-significant-digit rounding, maximum
relative difference 3e-15.

## Agricultural water

### Quantity and price

The quantity side is Shunkei's crop-level water accounting: per CropGBWater crop, country and
water source, a lambda coefficient in [0, 1] — the Ky-weighted mean of growth-stage
water-satisfaction ratios — for rainfed green water, irrigated green water and irrigated blue
water, with a VMR pair reported beside the green components, never netted against them. The
price side is the value of the crop: lambda times a rainfed/irrigated value basis gives the
water-attributable share of that value.

### Valuation

`agriculture_basis_from_crop_values` rebuilds the author's value preparation (his Code/1-4) on
the account's own crop values. FAOSTAT items map to CropGBWater crops through his
correspondence, many-to-one items sum, the two shared items (Wheat and Millet) allocate by his
SPAM production-quantity weights within country and item, and SPAM rainfed/irrigated shares
split each crop-country value into `basis_rain` and `basis_irr`, with his own split-status
labels where the SPAM row is absent or zero. One departure is documented in the docstring: an
all-missing group stays missing instead of his na.rm zero, because the account's table carries
genuine gaps and a fabricated zero would read as measured.

`agriculture_gep_from_lambda` is his final stage (Code/5): the three lambda-times-basis
products, their VMR pair, and `GEP_total` as the rowwise sum over the three components with
missing treated as zero — replicated from the author, partial totals included.
`aggregate_agriculture_gep_to_country` is his sum-if-any country aggregation.

The replication and the account run are not the same calculation. The test suite feeds the two
functions the author's own theta x GPV 2020 basis in thousand current US$ and reproduces his
September 21 crop-country and country results within measured float-reordering noise. The
`agriculture_water` task instead feeds the account's 2019 commercial crop-provision values in
current USD, with the CWoN rental rate already applied, so no theta and no rental
re-application, split rainfed/irrigated by his SPAM shares. The 2019 substitution is the
account's decision, not his output. His upstream lambda, SPAM, crop-mapping and theta
derivations are taken as given, and matching his final-stage outputs proves fidelity, not
correctness.

2019 is the monetary year only; the physical inputs carry their own vintages. The SPAM shares
are SPAM 2020 v2r2 (his Code/1-3, the Harvard Dataverse release), and lambda is built on a
representative 365-day daily ET0 profile averaged over 2018-2022 (his Code/3).

Under the meeting convention this value is an intermediate contribution: the basis is the
crop-provision GEP itself, so the agricultural-water figure is the water-attributable share of
value already counted in crop provision. It is reported for attribution and is never added to a
GEP total beside crop provision.

Coverage is disclosed rather than repaired. Items with no correspondence row stay out of the
basis and are written to `agriculture_unmapped_items.csv` — rice is the largest. Crop-country
values whose SPAM row is absent or zero stay unsplit and carry their status. Split basis rows
with no lambda coefficients are written to `agriculture_missing_coefficients.csv`, and
`agriculture_coverage.csv` summarizes the value at each stage.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `water_supply` service:

- `water_supply_cwon_hydro_wealth_path`, the CWoN `hydro_wealth_cd` table, with a `_source_url`
  row for the World Bank reproducibility archive and a `_source_archive_member` row naming the
  file inside it.
- `water_use_efficiency_input_path`, the raw AQUASTAT export, with a `_source_url` row for the
  AQUASTAT data API.
- `water_use_withdrawal_path`, the withdrawal table.
- `water_use_agriculture_path` and `water_use_all_sector_path`, the drive's committed per-country
  tables, held as comparison anchors.
- `water_supply_agriculture_lambda_path`, `water_supply_agriculture_spam_path` and
  `water_supply_agriculture_correspondence_path`, the author's pinned processed tables under
  `agriculture/shunkei_e229f881/` in base_data, with a `water_supply_agriculture_source` row
  and a provenance README beside the files.
- `water_supply_crop_values_path`, the commercial crop country-item table in USD, blank by
  default: the task falls back to the crop_provision results registry, then to
  `water_supply_crop_values_relative_file` against the project directory. Reading the
  producer's own path removes the copy, not the staleness: the table is only as fresh as the
  last crop_provision run, so the agriculture figure's provenance includes the crop_provision
  run that wrote it, and a crop_provision change requires regenerating that table before this
  service's figure is quoted.

## Outputs

- `hydropower_rent.csv` from the `hydropower_rent` task.
- `aquastat_water_efficiency_cleaned.csv`, `water_use_gep_by_country_year.csv` and
  `water_use_components.csv` from the `water_use_components` task.
- `agriculture_by_country.csv` and `agriculture_by_crop_country.csv` from the
  `agriculture_water` task, with `agriculture_basis.csv`, `agriculture_coverage.csv` and the
  diagnostic tables (unmapped items, missing coefficients, unallocated shared value, unsplit
  statuses) beside them.
- `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` from `gep_calculation`, holding the r250 identifiers and
  attributes, `year`, the hydropower pair, the water-use value-added and domestic columns, the
  agriculture component columns (`water_use_agriculture_gep` with its rainfed/irrigated and VMR
  parts, and `water_use_irrigation_gep` now equal to the agriculture component), and
  `water_supply_gep`.

## Method constants

- `water_supply_hydropower_capitalization_rate = 0.04` in `es_parameters`, the rate CWoN
  capitalized their wealth figure with.

  ⚠ **This is not the account's discount rate and must not be harmonized onto it.** The account
  discounts future benefits at 2 percent, with sensitivity at 1 and 3. This rate is doing the
  opposite job: CWoN published a *capitalized* wealth figure, and hydropower GEP is the annual
  rent inside it, so the module runs their capitalization backwards. Inverting with any rate but
  the one they capitalized with returns a rent CWoN never capitalized — the number would become
  wrong in the act of making it look consistent. The two quantities share a word and nothing else.
  The consistency gate knows the difference and reports both.
- `HYDROPOWER_HORIZON_YEARS = 100`, the CWoN capitalisation horizon.
- `HYDROPOWER_GEP_YEAR = 2019`, the wealth column the rent is read from. Current USD equals real
  2019 USD in the 2019 base year, and this is the only variant that covers Venezuela.
- `HYDROPOWER_REFERENCE_EXCLUDED`, seventeen iso3 codes set to NaN to reproduce the reference:
  AZE, BGR, DOM, GRC, GTM, HTI, KAZ, LBR, MAR, MKD, NIC, POL, PRT, SLV, TJK, UKR and ZAF.
- `WATER_USE_YEARS = (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015)`, the AQUASTAT survey years the calculation keeps.
- `WATER_USE_EFFICIENCY_SERIES`, `WATER_USE_COUNTRY_RENAMES`, `WATER_USE_ISO_LOOKUP` and
  `WATER_USE_REGIONS_DROPPED`, which reproduce script 02's name surgery verbatim.

## Taken as given

CWoN's own hydropower wealth estimate, and the AQUASTAT efficiency and withdrawal series.

## What is open

The seventeen excluded countries are the largest open item. The reference output leaves them empty
although the CWoN wealth table values them, and no available material explains the drop, because
the 2026 script is not on the drive and the package lacks its raw workbook. The exclusion is
encoded to reproduce the reference, the reason is an ask on the deck, and changing the list is a
reviewed-commit decision.

The drive's per-country water-use tables are not this calculation's outputs and are held as anchors
rather than adopted. The agriculture table equals 1000 times `GEP_total` from the crop-water
valuation whose scripts are now identified and pinned: the Shunkei repository this module
replicates. The all-sector table was computed on a newer AQUASTAT
vintage with the appendix's deflate-to-2015 step, and only 3 of 183 countries reproduce from the
staged inputs, with a median committed to computed-at-2019 ratio of 0.36 over a range of 0 to 1.25.

Script 02's lookup countries keep their AQUASTAT names, so their efficiency and withdrawal rows
share an iso code but never a country name. The merge leaves them as half-rows with no products,
including USA, RUS and TUR. The anchor commits that behaviour and the port reproduces it.

`water_supply_gep` stays the hydropower component alone. How, and whether, the water-use and
agriculture components combine with it is the account's subgroup question, flagged on the deck.
The water-use chain's domestic calculation is preserved and published unchanged; what stays open
for municipal water is scope and method — the withdrawal series mixes municipal with industrial
use, and the price follow-up is assigned on the review — not the existence of a calculation.

The domestic raw-water price is still implied by the OLD premium-based irrigation GEP, not by
the agriculture component that replaced that column in the published table. Repricing domestic
water on the new component is its own reviewed change, not a side effect of this one.

The agriculture correspondence covers 28 crops. The account's crop table carries value on items
outside it — rice is the largest single item — which the author's method never valued and this
port therefore leaves out of the basis, disclosed in `agriculture_unmapped_items.csv`. Whether
the correspondence should be extended is an author question, not a port decision.
